Incorporating the August 2021 Beige Book (published around the Sept. 22 FOMC), the tone should be tempered relative to the SLOOS-only read. While the FOMC statement remains highly accommodative and the July SLOOS shows easing terms and stronger loan demand (supporting active credit transmission), the Beige Book reported a downshift to a “moderate” growth pace amid Delta headwinds, widespread labor shortages, rising wages, and broad-based price pressures tied to supply-chain bottlenecks. These regional insights suggest constraints on the pace of activity and more persistent cost pressures than “transitory” alone implies.

Net: still mildly positive given supportive financial conditions and credit, but less so after accounting for Beige Book’s cooling momentum and capacity constraints; risks to the outlook are more two-sided. Adjusting down slightly from 0.35.
